issues.legal_issue: An absolute bequest in an earlier part of a will cannot be cut down by a later inconsistent disposition of the same property.
material_facts: An earlier clause of the will vested the property jointly in the testator’s wife and elder daughter, without words limiting their interest, and provided that either would become the exclusive owner if the other died first.
A later clause of the same will purported to give different portions of the same property to other descendants after the wife and daughter died.
The court found that the earlier clause created an absolute interest and that the later disposition could not be reconciled with it.
issues.conclusion: The earlier clause created an absolute interest in the wife and daughter. The later clause disposing of the same property was ineffective, while the rest of the will remained operative.
issues.legal_principle: A will must be read as a whole, and its clauses should be harmonized where possible. If an earlier clause clearly gives an absolute interest and a later clause concerning the same property conflicts with that disposition, the earlier absolute disposition prevails and the later clause is ineffective. The Court applied Ramkishorelal v. Kamal Narayan, 1963 Supp (2) SCR 417, as approved and followed in Mauleshwar Mani v. Jagdish Prasad, (2002) 2 SCC 468; those authorities also refer to Sahebzada Mohd. Kamgar Shah v. Jagdish Chandra Deo Dhabal Deo, Radha Sundar Dutta v. Mohd. Jahadur Rahim, and Rameshwar Bakhsh Singh v. Balraj Kuar. No statutory provision was relied on to decide this issue.

rule.if: will_construction_case and earlier_bequest_absolute and later_bequest_same_property and later_bequest_conflicts

predicates.will_construction_case: The dispute requires a court to construe the clauses of a will.
predicates.earlier_bequest_absolute: An earlier clause of the will gives a beneficiary an absolute interest in property without limiting that interest.
predicates.later_bequest_same_property: A later clause of the will purports to dispose of the same property to another beneficiary.
predicates.later_bequest_conflicts: The later disposition cannot be harmonized with the earlier absolute disposition.
predicates.later_bequest_ineffective: The later disposition does not take effect against the earlier absolute disposition.

issues.definition: When a will-construction case involves an earlier absolute bequest and a later conflicting disposition of the same property that cannot be harmonized, the later disposition is ineffective.
